newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin not to accept yields over 16.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin not to accept yields over 16.5 pct.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry said on Wednesday high interbank rates made budget deficit refinancing expensive, but that it would not accept average yields over 16.5 percent in state securities auctions.

"Yields in our auctions are rising too high...we now consider an average yield of some 16.5 percent as the top level where we will accept bids in coming auctions," Marian Horvath, head of the State Assets and Liabilities Department, told Reuters.

Earlier on Wednesday, the average yield in an auction of five-week treasury bills hit 16.048 percent, after it had sold one-year state bonds worth 2.4 billion crowns on Tuesday at an average yield of 16.812 percent.

The 1997 state budget plans deficit refinancing at an interest rate of some nine percent, while the ministry has been accepting an average 15 percent rates since the beginning of this year due to a money market liquidity shortage which pushed interbank rates to around 30 percent.

Horvath added the ministry was planning to introduce several new measures to help find cheaper funds for covering state budget deficit, which he said totalled 17.790 billion crowns as of July 8, 1997.
"We want to widen the range of investors allowed to take part in auctions of state securities," Horvath said.
At present, only banks, securities traders and insurance companies are allowed to buy state securities.
But, he said, the ministry is now working on material that should allow companies, or even citizens, to buy both state bonds and treasury bills.
"We are considering issuing non-publicly traded state paper with a status of bearer security, and we plan to start with an issue of one-year state bonds by the end of this year," Horvath said.
He added the ministry planned to offer yields some "one or two percent higher than the best interest rate at a commercial bank" to make state securities attractive for potential small investors.
